2609.39877.title: Algorithmic Recourse Under Competition
2609.39877.paper_summary: Algorithmic recourse provides individuals who have received undesirable outcomes from machine learning models with suggestions for minimum-cost improvements to achieve the desired outcome. A central assumption when computing recourse is that the decision rule remains fixed throughout the recourse implementation phase. We challenge this assumption in settings where individuals compete for limited resources. In such settings, widespread recourse implementation can change the acceptance threshold even when the scoring model that is used to evaluate individuals remains the same. This change in acceptance threshold can, in turn, invalidate the original recourse recommendations (i.e., following the recourse may not lead to the desired outcome). To address this problem, we introduce a framework called recourse under competition that jointly optimizes for recommendation recipients and the recommended score target they need to satisfy to balance the recourse cost and post-shift validity among initially rejected individuals. We develop an algorithm based on the Implicit Function Theorem and empirically analyze its performance. Experiments on synthetic and real datasets show that personalized score targets can achieve higher validity, albeit at a higher cost. In contrast, common score targets generally offer favorable cost-validity trade-offs for lower to medium validity values.
2609.39877.paper_summary_zh: 算法性補救為那些從機器學習模型中獲得不理想結果的個體提供最低成本改善建議，以達成所期望的結果。計算補救時的一個核心假設是決策規則在補救實施階段保持不變。我們在個體為有限資源競爭的情境中挑戰這一假設。在這種情境下，廣泛的補救實施可以改變接受閾值，即使用於評估個體的評分模型保持不變。接受閾值的變化反過來可能使原始的補救建議失效（即，遵循補救可能不會導致所期望的結果）。為了解決這個問題，我們提出了一個名為競爭下的補救的框架，該框架共同優化推薦接收者和他們需要滿足的推薦分數目標，以平衡補救成本和最初被拒個體的後移有效性。我們基於隱函數定理開發了一個算法並對其性能進行了實證分析。在合成和真實數據集上的實驗顯示，個性化的分數目標可以實現更高的有效性，儘管成本較高。相比之下，常見的分數目標通常為較低到中等有效性值提供有利的成本-有效性權衡。
